stem: When did Sir Stafford Cripps arrive in Delhi?
expl: America and China put pressure on Britain to grant independence to India. As a result, the then British Prime Minister Winston Churchill announced the Cripps Mission on 11 March 1942. On 23 March 1942, the Cripps Mission reached Delhi, headed by Sir Stafford Cripps.

expl: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, in his book India Wins Freedom, said about the proposals that the British delegation of the Cripps Mission was to place before Indians: “The Cripps offer really gave us nothing. If we accepted his offer, we might have cause to rue it in the future. The war had given India an opportunity for achieving her freedom. We must not lose it by depending upon a mere promise.”

stem: Who viewed the Cripps proposal as a 'post-dated cheque upon a crashing bank'?
expl: After the Japanese forces captured Rangoon, under pressure from the United States, the British Government decided to send Sir Stafford Cripps (a member of the British Cabinet) to India, so that a solution could be found through talks with Indian leaders. Cripps stayed in India for three weeks (March–April 1942) and, after discussions with Indian leaders, announced his proposals as a draft. Mahatma Gandhi described it as a “post-dated cheque”; according to Sarvepalli Gopal’s book Jawaharlal Nehru: A Biography, the words “on a crashing bank” were added by a journalist.
